repeat1.interpretation: The deterministic browser topology is exactly one topology emitted by Blender for the same one-pass graph. A separate Blender run differed by 6 vertices and 8 faces, demonstrating native OpenVDB scheduling variability before downstream repeats.

repeat2.interpretation: This is the first persistent topology divergence. The deterministic GN-VM result is outside both recorded Blender schedules, so native OpenVDB variability is an amplifier but does not explain the entire residual. The controlled input lattice differs at one of 131,279 signs; durable diagnostics localize that sign to a compiler-sensitive n-gon triangulation/BVH coincident-hit tie.

performance: Volume Cube density evaluation accounts for roughly 98-99% of each pass; nearest-surface and raycast field evaluation, not surface-net meshing, is the dominant cost.
completedCrossGridExperiment: tools/fixtures/watertight-cross-grid/evidence.json proves reciprocal byte-exact 131279-value sampling and identical meshing. Equal-count pass-one sources differ at 80 signs, isolating the cascade to live source generation/scheduling.
